segment_exposures.note: Decaying to ~70% by 2029 as custom ASICs scale
Spectrum-X — 0 to ~18% DC share in ~24 months

financials.notes: TTM = fiscal year ended Jan 31 2026. Fwd = analyst consensus FY27 (calendar 2026). Price as of May 8 2026 ATH.

thesis.short: NVIDIA captures ~$241B of theoretical 2026 flow across GPUs (~80% share) and Spectrum-X networking. Consensus already models 70%+ revenue growth, so FCR sits around 1.6 — flow technically exceeds the implied jump. Priced rather than higher-conviction because the 92%→68% share decay through 2029 is real: Broadcom-designed ASICs (Google TPU, Meta MTIA, AWS Trainium) and AMD MI355X are taking second-source slots, and the market is already paying for whatever durability emerges.
thesis.risks: Custom-ASIC share erosion in accelerators; HBM4 supply allocation timing; export-control shocks; multiple compression on any single guide miss.

segment_exposures.note: MI355X / MI400X scaling. Second-source share with Microsoft, Meta, Oracle

financials.notes: Q1 2026 revenue $10.25B (beat $9.89B); data center $5.8B (+57% YoY); stock +66% YTD 2026; Lisa Su doubled long-term forecast.

thesis.short: The MI300/350 ramp and CPU pull-through from Intel's structural weakness lift AMD's hyperscaler-attributable flow to ~$24.5B for 2026. Consensus already models $17B of revenue growth, so FCR sits around 1.4 — just below the Higher conviction threshold. The story is real but execution-dependent: every quarter that data center revenue prints at or above guidance compounds the multiple, every miss compresses it.
thesis.risks: Hyperscaler second-source slot durability vs. NVIDIA's Blackwell/Rubin cadence; foundry capacity allocation at TSMC competing with Apple/NVIDIA/Broadcom; macro CPU demand stickiness as EPYC matures.

financials.notes: Q1 FY26 revenue $19.3B (+29% YoY); AI semiconductors $8.4B (+106%); Q2 guide $22B; FY26 implied $85B; mgmt envisions AI chip rev >$100B by FY27 backed by $73B backlog.

thesis.short: The flagship custom-ASIC franchise (Google TPU + Meta MTIA + emerging AWS/Microsoft engagements) plus Tomahawk switching silicon gives Broadcom ~$29B of theoretical 2026 flow. Consensus already models $25B of revenue growth. FCR around 1.2 sits squarely in Priced. The bull case (AI revenue >$100B by FY27) is partly built into the 35x multiple; the bear case is that custom-ASIC wins are lumpy and a single hyperscaler reverting to NVIDIA could compress estimates fast.
thesis.risks: Customer concentration in custom-ASIC business; potential NVDA share defense via Spectrum-X eroding Tomahawk's whitebox advantage; VMware integration drag on operating leverage.

segment_exposures.note: Gaudi 3 + Falcon Shores. Long-shot accelerator share — includes Intel/Other bucket

financials.notes: Stock +129% YTD 2026 to $130.57 ATH; Q1 2026 revenue $13.6B (+7% YoY); FY26 estimate $59.43B (+12.44%).

thesis.short: Auto-FCR math says Higher conviction (~1.7) because the 4% 'Intel/Other' share against $288B GPU spend implies ~$11.5B of theoretical flow against ~$6.6B implied growth. The flow attribution is generous: Gaudi 3 and Falcon Shores have not won meaningful hyperscaler share at scale, and the 4% includes 'Other' rather than reflecting confirmed Intel design wins. Overriding to Watching until accelerator share materializes — the foundry turnaround narrative drives the stock more than data center silicon today.
thesis.risks: Gaudi 4 / Falcon Shores execution risk; foundry losses dwarfing data center upside; CPU share concession to AMD continues.

segment_exposures.note: HBM3E shipping at scale; HBM4 sampling. US-domestic supply premium

financials.notes: Stock +124% YTD 2026, +700% over past year. Q1 FY26 record $13.64B; Q2 guide $18.7B at 68% GM; FY26 consensus ~$76B; 2026 HBM supply sold out.

thesis.short: The HBM supercycle is real and Micron's 20% segment share is structural (US-domestic supply premium matters under CHIPS Act and export-control regimes). But consensus already models a $26B revenue jump while the hyperscaler-attributable memory flow only accounts for ~$13.6B at Micron's share. FCR around 0.5 says the market is paying for more growth than the hyperscaler capex line can supply by itself. Auto-FCR Lower conviction; bull counter is that HBM TAM and DRAM blended ASPs lift all boats.
thesis.risks: Cycle peak ASP normalization; HBM4 yield ramp at Boise/Singapore; consensus revision risk if any quarter prints below the parabolic curve.

thesis.short: HBM monopoly with capacity sold out through 2026 and HBM4 allocated through 2028. Theoretical 2026 memory flow ($36B at 53% share) is meaningful but consensus already prices in $82B of revenue growth ($68B TTM → $150B FWD) thanks to a 700%+ stock run. Auto-FCR flags Lower conviction; the flip-side argument is that HBM TAM extends well beyond hyperscaler capex (enterprise AI, smartphones, autos).
thesis.risks: Cycle peak risk if HBM ASPs normalize 2027+; Samsung HBM3E/4 qualification at NVDA closing the share gap; geopolitical exposure (KRW/USD, Korea-China relations).

thesis.short: Samsung is too big and too diversified for the FCR framework to read well: hyperscaler memory at 27.5% share gives ~$18.7B of theoretical flow, but Samsung's $135B implied total revenue growth dilutes it to FCR ~0.14 (auto Lower conviction).
